clue.text: Avoid measure taken by fellow players

parts.note: a side is a team, a body of fellow players
a step is a measure or action taken, as in 'take steps'

explanation.surface: Someone takes a measure that their team-mates agree to.
explanation.walkthrough: The charade is in answer order: the team comes first, the measure second, although the clue names the measure first; 'taken by' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodge a problem is to step aside from it, a synonym for evading.

clue.text: Medical application hazardous to Scott

explanation.surface: A medical treatment is somehow dangerous to a man named Scott.
explanation.walkthrough: Scott is the Antarctic explorer Robert Falcon Scott, whose ships faced floating sea ice packed together; the same phrase names a cold compress.
explanation.definitionFit: A bag of ice laid on an injury is a cold compress; packed floating sea ice endangered polar expedition ships.

clue.text: Settle for this sable — it's fashionable

indicators.note: something fashionable has been fashioned, shaped anew, so these letters are remade into another order

explanation.surface: Someone decides on a sable fur because it is in vogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashionable' normally means stylish; read as 'able to be fashioned' it tells you to rework THIS SABLE. 'for' and 'it's' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle something is to fix or set it up firmly, a synonym.

clue.text: Angry words from sun god overwhelmed by the sea

indicators.note: something overwhelmed by the sea is engulfed, so the god's name sits inside the word for the sea

parts.note: the tide is the sea as it rises and falls
Ra is the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: A sun god, swamped by the waves, shouts in fury.
explanation.definitionFit: A long outburst of angry speech is a harangue or rant.

clue.text: The kingdom's spies are housed in London

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the lords themselves, who sit in the House of Lords at Westminster

parts.note: to spy is to peer, look closely
of the realm means belonging to the kingdom

explanation.surface: A nation's secret agents are lodged in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spies' looks like a noun for secret agents but is the verb 'looks'. The definition is cryptic: the House of Lords in London is where these nobles sit.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the nobility sit in Parliament's upper chamber, the House of Lords at Westminster.

clue.text: The wood-louse thus identified, in one case

indicators.note: the word for thus goes in the middle of one and case

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
a pod is a seed case
so means thus

explanation.surface: A wood-louse has been identified, in one particular instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in one case' reads as 'in one instance', but it is the container: SO goes inside I + POD. 'identified' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Wood-lice are crustaceans of the order whose members have legs all alike, a classic example.

clue.text: Form of nitre a leftist hid underground

indicators.note: a form of a word is a new shape of it, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a red is a left-winger, a communist

explanation.surface: A left-winger buried some saltpetre in a hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form of' reworks NITRE into INTER, then RED follows. 'a' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To put a body in a grave is to bury it, hiding it in the earth.

clue.text: Stipulation that Dutch anarchist is imprisoned

indicators.note: what is imprisoned is shut inside, so the little word sits within the anarchist

parts.note: the Provos were a 1960s Dutch anarchist movement, each member a Provo

explanation.surface: A condition is laid down that a Dutch radical be jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: PROVO, a member of a 1960s Amsterdam anarchist group, takes IS inside. 'that' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A clause adding a condition to an agreement is a stipulation.

clue.text: Apollyon breaking down reeds around Ilium

indicators.note: the shuffled reeds go around the city's name
reeds breaking down fall apart, so their letters are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: Ilium is the Latin name for Troy

explanation.surface: A demon shatters the reeds around the ancient city of Ilium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking down' turns REEDS into DESER, which goes 'around' TROY to give DES-TROY-ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Apollyon, the angel of the bottomless pit in Revelation, has a name meaning 'the destroyer' in Greek.

clue.text: We try to get his lights for the dog

definitions.text: We try to get his lights

explanation.surface: Someone tries to fetch a man's lamps for the dog.
explanation.walkthrough: Solvers like us try to get the compiler's lights, the answers in the grid, while the second sense is the gundog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The compiler of a crossword makes the lights solvers fill in; a pointer-like gundog breed shares the name.

clue.text: Revised often, so succeeded shortly afterwards

indicators.note: a revised text has been altered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in family trees

explanation.surface: Something was revised many times and soon came out right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revised' reworks OFTEN + SO into EFTSOON, then S follows. The held clue had an extra 'I' not on the page.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for soon after, again, used by Spenser and in pastiche.

clue.text: Cutting remarks about a party in the West Indies

indicators.note: the remarks go about, around, the other letters

parts.note: barbs are wounding, cutting remarks
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Sharp words are exchanged over a party in the Caribbean.
explanation.definitionFit: The island nation lies in the Caribbean, part of the West Indies.

clue.text: Weapon used to give a smart blow? That's right

parts.note: a rap is a sharp knock
i.e. stands for 'that is'

explanation.surface: Asked which weapon gives a sharp blow, someone confirms it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's' looks like a reply but is i.e., Latin id est, 'that is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A light slender sword for thrusting is a duelling weapon.

clue.text: Initially evil-hearted, pelt wild geese in flight

indicators.note: evil-hearted is read as having that letter put at the heart of the next word

parts.note: a pelt is an animal skin

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A wicked person throws things at wild geese flying overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evil-hearted' looks like 'wicked', but it puts E at the heart of SKIN; 'pelt' is the noun hide, not the verb throw.
explanation.definitionFit: A flock of wild geese flying in formation has its own collective noun.

clue.text: Desire a name for this vehicle?

definitions.text: Desire a name for this vehicle?

parts.words: Desire a name for this vehicle?
parts.note: Tennessee Williams's play is titled after a tram named Desire, so the vehicle bears that name

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a car could be called Desire.
explanation.walkthrough: Recall Tennessee Williams's play 'A ... Named Desire': the vehicle in its title is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An American tram running on city rails, made famous by Williams's play title.

clue.text: Extend politician's part of the office

parts.note: to extend a hand or invitation is to offer it
a Tory is a Conservative politician

explanation.surface: A politician's role in the office is being extended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'office' is not a workplace but a church service; the offertory is a section of the Mass.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Communion service, the stage when bread, wine and alms are presented is a liturgical section.

clue.text: Try brush with feathers

parts.note: a brush is a light touch
down is soft fine feathers

explanation.surface: Someone tests a brush made of feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' is the score in rugby (or American football), not an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Grounding the ball over the line scores in American football; a rugby try is the same act.

clue.text: The grill is free in Garrick's first club

indicators.note: the word for free goes inside the other letters
first takes the opening letter of the following name

parts.note: an iron is a golf club
to rid is to free

explanation.surface: The grill-room is free at a club founded on the actor Garrick.
explanation.walkthrough: The Garrick is a London gentlemen's club, but here only its first letter G is used, with RID placed inside G + IRON.
explanation.definitionFit: A gridiron is a metal frame of bars for broiling, a grill.

clue.text: Select stretch of river, letting out a wild cheer

indicators.note: letting out a means dropping that letter from the river word

parts.note: a reach is a straight stretch of river

indicators.note: wild means the letters of cheer run riot in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone picks a stretch of river and lets out a loud cheer.
explanation.walkthrough: REACH 'letting out' A leaves RECH; 'wild' rearranges CHEER into ERCHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Recherché means choice or exquisite, carefully sought out.

clue.text: Scots fellow, the first to support the pretender?

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the person who does it, a backer of the claimant

parts.note: carl is a Scots word for a man or fellow
1st, written with the figure as the letter I, means first

explanation.surface: A Scotsman is the first to rally behind a claimant to the throne.
explanation.walkthrough: The pretender is Don Carlos, nineteenth-century claimant to the Spanish throne; his followers took his name. 'the first' is 1ST with the 1 read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers of Don Carlos backed his claim to the Spanish throne as rightful king.

clue.text: One purchasing a cow-shed, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word for the shed is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a byre is a cow-shed

explanation.surface: Someone is shopping for a cow-shed.
explanation.walkthrough: BYRE, a cowshed, and the answer are pronounced alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone making a purchase is a customer or purchaser.

clue.text: Impress deeply in French accent

parts.note: en is French for in
the grave is an accent, as in è

explanation.surface: Someone makes a strong impression with a French accent.
explanation.definitionFit: To carve or etch a design into a surface is to impress it deeply.

clue.text: Strike in the counter service.

explanation.surface: A strike is called in the counter service.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is to hit or batter; the other is self-service food laid out on a counter.
explanation.definitionFit: To buffet is to hit repeatedly; a buffet is food served from a counter or sideboard.

clue.text: Message some 9 ran down to deliver

indicators.note: some means only part of these words is used, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: 9 stands for the answer at 9 across, the dog and compiler, followed by the words ran down

explanation.surface: Some dogs ran down to deliver a message.
explanation.walkthrough: Substitute the answer at 9 across, then read the run across 'settER RAN Down'. 'to deliver' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An errand is a trip made to deliver a message or do a job.

clue.text: Coarse fodder's approximate length of life

parts.note: a rough figure is an approximate one
age is the length of one's life

explanation.surface: Some animal feed is only roughly as old as claimed.
explanation.definitionFit: Fibrous food that aids digestion is bulky coarse feed.

clue.text: Eric and Rita break their principles

indicators.note: to break the names is to smash them and reassemble the letters in another order

explanation.surface: Eric and Rita abandon their beliefs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' rearranges ERIC + RITA; 'and' and 'their' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Standards by which things are judged are principles or yardsticks.

clue.text: Concerning bloomers in extremely factual exam?

indicators.note: extremely takes the letters at the extremes, the first and last, of factual

parts.note: an oral is a spoken exam

explanation.surface: An exam question that is factual about underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' suggests knickers but means flowers; F and L are the first and last letters of 'factual'.
explanation.definitionFit: Floral means relating to flowers, which bloom.

clue.text: Palm-oil rejected by knight on board

indicators.note: rejected means the oil word is turned back on itself

parts.note: attar is a fragrant oil from rose petals
N is the knight's symbol in chess notation, on the chessboard

explanation.surface: A knight on a ship turns down some palm oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Palm-oil' looks like one thing, but the hyphen splits the definition from ATTAR, which 'rejected' turns round to RATTA.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing palm whose stems are used for canes and wicker furniture.

clue.text: A revolting type, was Fletcher Christian!

definitions.text: A revolting type, was Fletcher Christian!

parts.words: A revolting type, was Fletcher Christian!
parts.note: Fletcher Christian led the 1789 revolt on HMS Bounty, so he was one who rose against his captain

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that Fletcher Christian was a disgusting person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' means disgusting on the surface, but here means rebelling: Christian led the mutiny on the Bounty.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor who rebels against his officers is a rebel at sea.
